messages:
Rachael (Security): Heads up — AcmeCorp is asking for BYOK + HSM-proxy pattern for prod. We need to scope RBAC, audit retention, and a cross-region failover pattern. Questions: 1) minimal operator role for their tenant (what exact kms actions?), 2) audit log retention & fields for SOC2 / PCI checks, 3) KMS integration pattern for cross-region HSM fallback. @Tom (Infra) @Cheng please weigh in. :eyes:

Tom (Infra): My quick take — avoid granting broad CreateKey in our acct. Use an import-ext-key workflow where tenant generates key material and we import to a dedicated per-tenant HSM slot. Minimal role = KeyCustodian (kms:ImportKeyMaterial, kms:DescribeKey, kms:CreateGrant limited) + deny kms:ScheduleKeyDeletion. No ability to change audit config.

Tom (Infra): Example policy snippet (very minimal):

```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {"Effect":"Allow","Action":["kms:ImportKeyMaterial","kms:DescribeKey"],"Resource":"arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/tenant-*"},
    {"Effect":"Deny","Action":["kms:ScheduleKeyDeletion","kms:DisableKey"],"Resource":"*"}
  ]
}
```

Cheng: Audit retention: for SOC2 we need 12 months of searchable audit by default, legal sometimes asks for 2 years depending on customer contract. For PCI we should keep key-related audit events (ImportKeyMaterial, CreateGrant, ReEncrypt/GenerateDataKey, Rewrap) for 3 years if requested. Logs must include: key_id, requesting_principal, source_ip, operation, request_payload_hash (no key material), and correlation_id.

Cheng: For BYOK we cannot forward raw key material anywhere — only import confirmation hashes and attestation statements. Customer-facing audit exports can include consolidated events but must never include sensitive payloads.

audit-bot: Runbook linked — https://redwood.internal/runbooks/byok-hsm-proxy (contains onboarding checklist, required evidence for audits, RBAC matrix). :link:

Sam (oncall): If an import fails or HSM firmware alerts, what's triage on-call flow? Do we auto-revoke grants? What's break-glass?

Rachael (Security): Good call. Proposed: on import failure with integrity mismatch -> pause imports for the tenant, notify sec-pager + infra-pager, create incident ticket, and mark keys as quarantine (no degrant until manual review). Do NOT auto-revoke customer keys without manual approval unless we detect active compromise. Add step: preserve full audit trail and snapshot HSM attestations.

Tom (Infra): Operationally we'll use ephemeral attestation tokens from the HSM provider and mTLS to our proxy. Cross-region fallback: keep replicated key metadata and allow tenant to import to secondary HSM only after attestation check passes. We can automate failover if attestation == valid and operator-approved flag set. Sample proxy config (sketch):

```yaml
proxy:
  mtls: true
  attestation_ttl: 5m
  allowed_actions: [ImportKeyMaterial, DescribeKey, CreateGrant]
  audit_forward: false # default, enable per-customer export
```

Cheng: Open question for legal/compliance: can we expose operator role ARNs to customers for their own audits? I think we should provide only a fingerprint and an attest statement that lists the actions principals could perform. Full ARNs might be acceptable under NDA but prefer minimal leakage.

Rachael (Security): Agreed. We'll provide an attestable statement + signed policy snapshot. Also add a requirement: RBAC change requests (new KeyCustodian bindings) must go through a two-person review (sec + infra) and be logged with justification.

Tom (Infra): I'll draft the KeyCustodian role, policy, and the import-runbook changes tomorrow. Will also add API guardrails that prevent audit-level changes unless flagged by sec.

Cheng: I'll update the audit schema and retention matrix and send to legal for the 2-year vs 1-year decision.

Rachael (Security): Thanks — please @me when drafts are ready. I'll add the incident playbook step for quarantine and escalation. :thumbsup:

Sam (oncall): Copy — I'll add the playbook to oncall runbooks and test a simulated import-failure drill next week. :white_check_mark:

Tom (Infra): SGTM.

Rachael (Security): Cool — next steps: Tom drafts RBAC + proxy config, Cheng updates audit schema, Sam schedules drill, I'll own two-person review process doc. Looping legal after Cheng's doc.

Cheng: pinging legal once doc is ready.

Rachael (Security): Thanks all.
